"It may be true, as pointed out by learned counsel appearing for Respondent No.1,
that charge-sheet has already been filed.

sentences.text: It will be unfair to presume on our part that the Investigating Officer does not require Respondent No.1 for custodial interrogation for the purpose of further investigation.

sentences.text: Be that as it may, even assuming it a case where Respondent No.1 is not required for custodial interrogation, we are satisfied that the High Court ought not to have granted discretionary relief of anticipatory bail.

sentences.text: We are dealing with a matter wherein the original complainant (appellant herein) has come before this Court praying that the anticipatory bail granted by the High Court to the accused should be cancelled.

sentences.text:
To put it in other words, the 5 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:056304 2023:PHHC:056304 CRM-M-17408-2023 (O & M) ::6::
complainant says that the High Court wrongly exercised its discretion while granting anticipatory bail to the accused in a very serious crime like POCSO and, therefore, the order passed by the High Court granting anticipatory bail to the accused should be quashed and set aside.
sentences._hearing_file: Dharampal Singh vs State Of Punjab on 20 April, 2023.json

sentences.text:
In many anticipatory bail matters, we have noticed one common argument being canvassed that no custodial interrogation is required and,
therefore, anticipatory bail may be granted.
sentences._hearing_file: Dharampal Singh vs State Of Punjab on 20 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: There appears to be a serious misconception of law that if no case for custodial interrogation is made out by the prosecution, then that alone would be a good ground to grant anticipatory bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Dharampal Singh vs State Of Punjab on 20 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: Custodial interrogation can be one of the relevant aspects to be considered along with other grounds while deciding an application seeking anticipatory bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Dharampal Singh vs State Of Punjab on 20 April, 2023.json

sentences.text:
There may be many cases in which the custodial interrogation of the accused may not be required,
but that does not mean that the prima facie case against the accused should be ignored or overlooked and he should be granted anticipatory bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Dharampal Singh vs State Of Punjab on 20 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: The first and foremost thing that the court hearing an anticipatory bail application should consider is the prima facie case put up against the accused.
sentences._hearing_file: Dharampal Singh vs State Of Punjab on 20 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: Thereafter, the nature of the offence should be looked into along with the severity of the punishment.
sentences._hearing_file: Dharampal Singh vs State Of Punjab on 20 April, 2023.json

opennyai_summary.20_April_2023__facts:
2.  The brief facts of the case are that a complaint had been received in the office of the Bureau of Investigation, Punjab, to the effect that Kuljinder Singh, Baljinder Singh and others had filed a Dharampal Singh vs State Of Punjab on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72400919/
1 CWP-13159- 2020 (O & M) titled as 'Kuljinder Singh and others Vs. State of Punjab and others' and CWP No.8552-2020 (O & M) titled as 'Baljinder Singh and others versus State of Punjab and others'
before the Punjab and Haryana High Court in which they had disclosed about the irregularities done by the 1 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:056304 2023:PHHC:056304 CRM-M-17408-2023 (O & M) ::2::
PSPCL at the time of recruitment of Assistant Linemen.
The High Court had passed an order dated 27.10.2022 to the effect that since there were allegations of fake experience certificates, etc. being accepted by PSPCL, the DIG/IG, Crime was to file an affidavit narrating the investigation conducted and also to examine the role of the officials/officers of PSPCL in accepting the alleged fake experience certificates.
On the basis of the order of the High Court, an investigation begun and the writ petitioners-Kuljinder Singh and Baljinder Singh were joined in the investigation.
Baljinder Singh got recorded a statement to the effect that in the month of October,
2019, PSPCL had advertised posts for the recruitment of the Assistant Linemen and he had applied for the same.
He had been called for counselling and had produced all his educational certificates.
However, he had not been selected as he was not having any experience certificate.
Thereafter, 29 writ petitioners had filed petitions before the High Court and on the basis of the orders passed in the said petitions, the experience certificates of Assistant Linemen were verified from the firms and directors who had issued the same.
opennyai_summary.20_April_2023__arguments:
3. The learned counsel for the petitioner contends that the allegation against the petitioner that he had obtained employment as Assistant Linemen in the PSPCL by providing fake and fictitious experience certificate is incorrect.
In fact, the petitioner has committed no offence whatsoever.
There are no specific allegations or attributions against the petitioner.
The petitioner had worked with M/s Grewal Electric Store, Gidarbaha from 2003 to 2007 for which his experience certificate was duly issued.
Therefore, as the petitioner was ready and willing to join investigation,
he was entitled to the grant of anticipatory bail.
opennyai_summary.20_April_2023__ANALYSIS:
6. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of 'Sumitha Pradeep Vs. Arun Kumar C.K. & Anr. 2022(4)
RCR (Criminal) 977', held that merely because custodial interrogation was not required by itself could not be a ground to grant anticipatory bail.
Custodial Dharampal Singh vs State Of Punjab on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72400919/
4
In the instant case, the allegations against the petitioner are of using a forged experience certificate to obtain Government employment.
Therefore, this conduct on the part of the petitioner cannot be condoned in any manner whatsoever.
opennyai_summary.20_April_2023__decision: 8. In view of the aforementioned discussion, I find no merit in the present petition and the same is dismissed.

opennyai_summary.final__facts:
Petitioner, who acted as a mediator in this marriage, introduced the complainant with Satwinder Singh, Manpreet Kaur and one old aged lady at Ludhiana.
It was alleged that petitioner along with co-accused used to dupe the innocent people on the pretext of false marriage.
In this way, petitioner along with other co- accused duped the complainant of Rs.7,50,000/-.
In the course of investigation, petitioner was arrested as a suspect on 16.05.2023.
opennyai_summary.final__arguments:
He is thus not entitled to concession of bail.
Investigation is complete, he is thus not required for custodial interrogation.
Bail allows an accused to maintain his freedom until his guilt or innocence is determined.
opennyai_summary.final__ANALYSIS:
Allegations against petitioner are a matter of trial at this stage.
Conclusion of trial is still likely to take long time as it is proceeding at a snail pace.
There is no probability of tampering with evidence as the same has already been seized by the investigating agency.
I am of the view that no useful purpose would be served to keep petitioner in further preventive custody in instant case.
